status: investigation only; no implementation handoff or production fencing authorized by this document
problem: Eight incomplete native sessions reserve 8 GiB although their retained files total about 59 KiB. Unknown outcomes must stay protected. Proving that a model never started is a different question from making retained storage incapable of future growth.
proposal: Retain exact session paths, contents, aliases and unknown outcomes. Investigate an actual complete charged-resource bound joined to a controller-produced visible-inode write fence before replacing the 1 GiB ordinary future-growth reservation with a bounded retained-data demand. A visible inventory and kernel leases/flags alone are insufficient (D14). Keep the configured 8 GiB byte budget, 16-session ceiling, filesystem floors, workflow budgets and controls unchanged.
observations: The deployed store has seven Claude and one Codex retained session; observed layouts contain only owned.json and lock, with one retired.json. No production changes were made for this investigation.

A disposable probe on this host acquired a read file lease with no writer, received EAGAIN with an open writable descriptor and with a writable mapping after its descriptor closed, and succeeded after the mapping closed. This is an observation, not proof of every syscall race or a permanent fence.
Linux file leases may be broken after notification/timeout. F_GETLEASE changes when a break is initiated. A lease alone is not durable write revocation.

A second disposable probe held an exclusive flock and a read lease on the same O_RDONLY empty lock after fchmod(0400). This resolves descriptor compatibility for the observed local Linux filesystem only.

A deterministic real lease-break probe let a child pass the write-open permission check, observed SIGIO, then changed the file to 0400. After releasing the lease the child appended successfully. F_GETLEASE had changed to F_UNLCK. Any proposal treating a finite lease plus mode changes as permanent writer revocation is rejected.
A disposable FS_IOC_ENABLE_VERITY attempt returned errno95/EOPNOTSUPP on this filesystem despite CONFIG_FS_VERITY=y. No superblock features or production files were changed.

Main helper finally closes the session lock before waiting for bridge/QEMU shutdown; its outer TemporaryDirectory cleanup follows later. Flock availability alone therefore cannot establish full helper/process settlement.

The actual native helper passed a disposable delayed-lock-open test: the write open returned after mode restriction and lease release, but creation of session data failed EACCES. Positive control created its temporary directory. This is a supported helper-path observation, not proof of every writer.

Complete native-provider-vm.py and provider-supervisor.py bytes were found in the saved original producer binary with SHA2567bbdd56d..., matching current helper hashes. This does not establish Rust binary source correspondence or original outcome/closure.

The frozen owner-host immutable probe remains unexecuted on the actual host kernel 7.0.0-30; this session lacks CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE and sudo requires the owner password. The pending owner request authorizes disposable tests only, never production fencing.

A managed disposable no-NIC ext4 guest running kernel 7.0.0-31 with guest UID0 passed six immutable cases: directory create/unlink refusal, new write-open refusal, existing writable-FD refusal, existing shared mapping SIGBUS, an open already waiting on a read-lease break refused after immutable transition, and a prefaulted writable shared mapping SIGBUS. Original fixture bytes survived. Original supervisor confirmed all descendants reaped. The host mounted nothing; no production native state was changed and no reservation was reduced. This is a different kernel and serial fixture evidence, not an actual host or concurrent inventory proof.

A subsequent disposable guest experiment exercised a multi-inode candidate under controlled mutation interleavings. Setting directory/file flags without recensus failed four of eight tests by accepting added entries, replacement file/directory inodes and changed contents. Rechecking named and held identities, full inventory and contents after directory fencing and after file fencing then passed ten tests, including a late existing-FD write, retained partial restrictions and UID1000 inode-owner flag-clearing refusal. All six earlier immutable cases remained passing; original supervisor verified descendant cleanup. No production custody producer, crash durability, exact-host support or accounting grant is established.

A further four-boundary disposable ext4 experiment fsynced the original fixture/oracle and selected flag subset, then syncfs, before its original supervisor SIGKILLed QEMU without a guest unmount. A fresh boot of the same verified image inode independently recovered the original directory/file identities and contents. Captured-only, directory-only and one-file states remained partial; the fully flushed flags survived. All eight original boot supervisors verified descendant cleanup, and each killed QEMU had an observed live/then-exited pidfd. This is guest termination after explicit filesystem flush, not host power-loss testing, an actual-host result or a production custody/accounting proof.

A real guest negative control kept an already-open unlinked writable inode outside the complete visible inventory. After every visible file and directory was immutable and every visible file retained an actual read lease, a subprocess grew the unlinked inode by 4096 logical and allocated bytes. Visible identities/content, immutable flags and read leases remained unchanged. This demonstrates that visible-only fencing is insufficient for reduced growth demand; it does not assert such a descriptor exists in production.

An unchanged fe2e7b1f source checkout rebuilt the preserved original producer executable byte for byte (SHA2567bbdd56d...) after preserving its logical source/target paths and supplying its observed phone telemetry build value via the existing supported override. Whole-file SHA256 and cmp agree; no sections were ignored and no ELF/source patch was applied. This establishes a known-source reproduction witness for that saved executable, not which executable launched each retained runtime or original resource/input/writer closure. See1902-original-producer-reproduction.json.

Read-only inspection of the eight retained owned.json audit references found three anchor-stable committed logs whose full committed digests match their anchors. Their 285 distinct recorded admitted resource paths were absent. None of the eight exact runtime names occurs in its referenced committed log; the canary has zero admitted resource identities. These are bounded observations, not an exact original launch/resource join, audit seal, complete resource closure or permission to reduce demand. See1902-retained-audit-correlation-observation.json.

glossary.retained_unknown: Original outcome remains unresolved. Fencing does not establish nonrelease, settlement, safe replay, review approval, merge or native conversation restoration.
glossary.resource_custody: Proposed resource-only disposition retaining original bytes and names under both a verified write fence and a complete verified charged-resource bound. It is not original execution provenance or native ownership transfer.
glossary.growth_reservation: Budget for all possible future writes charged to the retained runtime, including hidden/unlinked resources and any shared/control costs not covered by separate conservative demand. Visible retained data and bounded control metadata remain reserved even after genuine closure.
glossary.file_lease: Short-lived Linux kernel coordination against conflicting file opens/truncation. It does not replace directory permissions, all-writer ingress exclusion or a durable custody record.

decisions.decision: Preserve the original files and unknown outcome; introduce no original execution binding or body nonrelease claim.
decisions.why: Storage growth can be controlled without inventing historical execution certainty.

decisions.decision: Keep byte/count/resource ceilings and owner controls. Count every retained session toward max_sessions.
decisions.why: Changing growth demand must be backed by an actual fence, not a quota increase or a counter reset.

decisions.decision: Use a separate typed resource-only capability and record. It cannot convert into native/input/source/recovery or merge authority.
decisions.why: A smaller storage reservation must not enable replay of an uncertain request.

decisions.decision: Initial eligibility is metadata-only local Linux state: exact supported owned.json schema, empty lock, optional supported scope-retirement metadata, no exports/completion/cache/temp/result files, private directories, regular singly-linked owner files, bounded sizes and stable identities.
decisions.why: Existing variable data or unsettled result material requires its original recovery path. Unsupported state retains full conservative growth demand.

decisions.decision: Inspect by default. Apply only through an authenticated controller operation after reviewed implementation and normal deployment. Never let candidate code or model output request a zero-growth grant.
decisions.why: Filesystem custody is an administrative resource transition, not a model tool or ordinary workflow instruction.

decisions.decision: No zero-growth/small-retained reservation until every load-bearing thread below is resolved and actual producer/consumer fault tests pass.
decisions.why: File modes, PID absence, a free flock or a serialized report alone do not exclude existing or delayed writers.

decisions.decision: If this investigation continues, acquire the session flock through an O_RDONLY descriptor and reuse or duplicate that same open-file description for the regular-file lease. Never open an additional writable session lock as part of the proof. Exact IPC ownership and lifetime remain OT2.
decisions.why: A proof helper must not create the writable descriptor that its own writer census is intended to exclude.

decisions.decision: There is no executable un-fencing path in the initial proposed custody feature. Preserve original modes/history for a separately designed future recovery. No failure, timeout, restart, rollback or missing acknowledgement restores write access automatically.
decisions.why: The earlier OT5 wording could imply implementing recovery before the necessary original outcome/source/input authority exists.

decisions.decision: Reject chmod plus temporary file leases as a standalone permanent write fence. Supported historical writer-ingress exclusion is still a prerequisite and remains unproved. Do not hand this document off for implementation or reduce production reservations.
decisions.why: A real delayed open remained writable after chmod and lease release; permissions do not revoke already authorized opens.

decisions.decision: Investigate FS_IMMUTABLE_FL on the original session directory and every eligible regular file as the durable fence candidate. Chmod remains supplemental. D9 continues to reject leases plus permissions alone. Retain real read leases as a conservative preparation check; never infer a grant from lease expiry or from the six guest cases.
decisions.why: The disposable ext4 guest refused existing-FD, delayed-open and writable-mapping writes after the immutable transition; the same pending-open race defeated chmod alone. Directory and file immutability answer separate namespace and content-growth obligations.

decisions.decision: Require evidence for the exact deployed host kernel/filesystem and the final multi-file transition, not merely the declared guest kernel. Until the controller can establish the complete live fence and revalidate it at admission, preserve full ordinary growth reservation. Neither the owner disposable probe nor guest success authorizes production mutation.
decisions.why: The tested guest kernel is 7.0.0-31 while the observed host runs 7.0.0-30; serial syscall tests do not certify concurrent inventory stability, helper privilege boundaries or crash persistence.

decisions.decision: The proposed immutable transition must be performed by a narrowly scoped privileged controller outside candidate/model execution. Native workers and all supported older helpers must lack authority to clear the original filesystem immutable flags. No arbitrary path, shell, flag-clearing command or capability is exposed to the daemon/model. Exact installation, request authentication, kernel/user-namespace scope, root-owned policy, descriptor provenance and lost-controller lifetime remain OT1/OT2; no helper is installed by this investigation.
decisions.why: An ordinary same-UID chmod can undo a permission fence. The immutable candidate instead depends on a real kernel capability boundary, which must be established for the supported actors and cannot be inferred from one current process capability sample.

decisions.decision: Invalid custody restores full ordinary future-growth demand in the single shared accounting evaluator immediately; it never preserves an earlier credit to keep reported totals within the configured ceiling. Revalidate all credited sessions at controller startup/restart, host or policy compatibility change, every readiness/admission decision and before any custody/resume/retirement operation. If recomputed demand exceeds a ceiling, report an explicit overcommitted capacity hold, refuse all new model/build/native growth admissions and fence affected running workflows at their next original execution boundary. Existing resources retain their original ownership until checked teardown; a restored reservation is not proof that a process stopped. Allow only the existing bounded reconciliation/cleanup authority, preserving retained data and original outcomes. No counter reset, eviction, automatic un-fence or termination of unrelated processes.
decisions.why: Checking only the next proposed credit does not account for capacity already allocated using an invalid earlier credit. Conservative accounting must expose the resulting deficit and stop additional growth rather than hide it.

decisions.decision: Reject a visible-inventory immutable fence plus read leases as a complete resource-growth bound. Before reducing any original reservation, actual R authority must cover or independently bound unlinked inodes, mappings/descriptors, external scratch/copies, descendants and shared mutable controller metadata as well as named files. A privileged setter or intact journal cannot create this missing resource proof. Missing coverage retains full ordinary demand.
decisions.why: The real unlinked-inode control allocated 4096 bytes despite a fully verified visible fence and all visible read leases. The counted namespace is not the complete possible charged-resource population.

protocol_hypothesis.action: Under original native StateLock and the selected session lock, read exact runtime and alias inventory, original ownership bytes, file/directory device/inode/UID/modes/link counts/allocated bytes and supported controller registration. The selection is observational until all gates pass. Do not hold a workflow mutex/transaction while acquiring native locks. The selected session lock must be opened O_RDONLY for the exclusive flock, as specified in D7; a writable lock descriptor would conflict with its own read lease.

Prove or conservatively bound the complete original charged-resource population and every future growth route: visible/unlinked inodes, inherited/duplicated FDs, writable mappings, external scratch/copies, shared controller metadata, original/current helpers and descendants and delayed starts. Join actual original resource ownership/correlation to R proof. The D14 unlinked-writer counterexample rejects visible-only fencing even with leases; native locks, metadata-only names and creator PID absence are not closure. OT1/OT2 and the resource-boundary amendment block this step.

Obtain real read leases on read-only descriptors for every retained regular file, with isolated signal handling and bounded child lifetime. Refuse conflicting writers/mappings, lease-break requests and unsupported filesystems. A short-lived helper must retain original lock/descriptor custody and close on parent death; caller timeout is not proof it stopped. OT2 defines the exact guarantee and IPC protocol. These leases cover their exact visible inodes only. They cannot establish absence of unlinked or external resources and do not replace the D14 R producer.

Persist a bounded custody intent before the first restrictive transition, preserving original identity, content and flags for every selected inode. Provisional or partially fenced state still reserves full ordinary growth. Under the proposed D10 mechanism, fence the original directory against namespace mutation and every selected regular file against content mutation, without renaming paths or clearing preexisting flags. Exact ordering must cover writers racing directory fencing, file creation/unlink and preauthorized opens: recensus the same held directory, reject any new/replaced/unsupported entry, verify every selected inode/flag/content and retain uncertainty on a partial transition. Chmod alone is insufficient. OT1-OT3 must establish the actual atomicity, fsync and restart contract before this is implementation-ready. Bind and preserve the separate original R resource-bound context; completing these visible-inode operations alone cannot reduce demand (D14).

Commit a resource-only receipt only after actual durable fence verification AND complete live R resource-bound verification. Bind native root and directory/file identities, exact original ownership bytes/hash, original modes, supported writer/resource contract and operation ID. A copied row/report or intact receipt is not a capability and cannot reconstruct a lost original live proof. Lost reply retries the same operation; pending/incompatible or incomplete-resource state cannot lower demand. OT2/OT3/OT4 define actual capability lifetime, storage, integrity and fresh reconciliation before any credit.

Readiness and actual native admission use one evaluator. Before any reduced future-growth reservation, freshly validate the complete durable custody receipt and live original directory/file identities, inventory and immutable flags under the defined original native locks. A receipt, cached report or earlier syscall success alone cannot grant capacity. Retained bytes and bounded custody metadata remain reserved; provisional, missing, unsupported or invalid proof stays conservative/unknown. All retained sessions still count against 16. Include pending transfer reservations. OT4 defines exact units/formula, atomic proof-to-admission join and cross-version readers. Revalidate all previously credited sessions on the D13 triggers, not only the proposed next session. Report restored conservative demand even if it exceeds the existing ceiling; block new growth and retain original active-resource ownership through verified cleanup. Revalidate the D14 original charged-resource bound as well as named inode flags. Any uncovered hidden/external/shared cost retains separate conservative demand; a valid visible receipt cannot silently erase it.

All current constructors, resume, alias observation, host helpers, scope retirement, terminal retirement and pruning must recognize custody. Refuse resuming or mutating a held runtime. Preserve legacy data when ordinary terminal cleanup cannot settle it; no chmod-back shortcut or fake completion. Fresh unrelated runtimes may use genuinely available capacity through normal admission. OT1 and OT5 block this join.

Only after actual verified fence/accounting use normal persisted capacity wakeup. Do not change workflow stages, source evidence, ownership, instructions, progress clock, spent budgets or merge allowance. Report retained-unknown separately from model readiness and restored autoship. Subsequent guarded native progress is live acceptance, not something a fixture proves.

open_threads.question: Enumerate supported original/current native writers and privileged flag-clearing authorities. Establish the D12 kernel/user-namespace/capability boundary for all supported actors, the exact root-owned helper policy and authenticated request/descriptor protocol, including path/inode replacement and unsupported old helpers/controllers. Show how the immutable directory plus all-file transition excludes namespace and content growth after preparation locks/leases close. Same-UID permissions, a current PID capability sample and the serial guest observations are insufficient. Define the supported host kernel/filesystem gate. The actual unlinked-inode control in D14 defeats visible-only fencing even with read leases. Supply the original resource-ownership/correlation and complete charged-population bound before designing a credit-producing helper; do not infer hidden-resource absence from metadata-only names.
open_threads.trigger: Before implementation or any production fence
open_threads.blocks: Fence validity, reservation reduction and rollout.

open_threads.question: Define the actual descriptor and signal/helper lifetime protocol and multi-file transition: existing/inherited writers, dirty/prefaulted mappings, pending opens, directory mutation during fencing, inventory recensus, break handling, parent death, bounded wait and original cleanup ownership. Preserve full reservation through every partial transition; no automatic flag clearing. The six serial guest cases narrow the syscall question but do not settle concurrent capture or exact-host support.
open_threads.trigger: Before a kernel proof factory or positive fence test is accepted

open_threads.question: Define private custody record/ledger schemas, authority producer, immutable bidirectional receipt/event validation, storage admission/retention, prepare/fence/commit states and restart reconciliation. Do not mutate the original native authority epoch or fabricate an original execution binding. Preserve exact prior modes for a supported future recovery; no automatic un-fence.
open_threads.blocks: Crash safety and resource-only custody capability.

open_threads.question: Specify eligibility bounds and a conservative reservation formula covering retained allocated/logical data, bounded custody metadata, active/new session growth and pending transfers; all retained sessions count toward max_sessions. Supply the concrete shared evaluator and atomic proof-to-admission join for every growth consumer, including restart and host/policy compatibility changes. Implement D13 invalidation: any unverifiable custody restores full ordinary demand, reports overcommit if necessary, blocks further growth, and uses original execution/teardown authority for affected active work. Test an invalidated credit after a later session has actually consumed the recovered capacity. No missing row or failed probe defaults to zero. Apply D14: hidden/unlinked resources, external scratch and shared controller metadata must have verified bounds or retain their conservative charge; visible retained bytes alone cannot replace full demand.

Inventory and gate every reader/writer/retirement/resume path, including older helpers and rollback builds. Initial custody has no executable un-fence or original outcome recovery command (D8). Define conservative unsupported legacy/malformed custody behavior now and preserve modes/history for a separately verified future exit. A terminal workflow alone cannot discard held unknown state.
open_threads.trigger: Before public command enablement or accounting cutover
open_threads.blocks: Compatibility, protection of unknown outcomes and eventual recovery.

non_goals: No deletion, raw backup/copy/archive, byte loss, original-path rename or source outcome relabeling.
No conversion to original execution provenance, no body replay permission, no owner pause/hold removal, quota increase, free-space floor override or accounting reset.
No claim to protect against a malicious owner/root administrator; explicitly bound supported trusted controllers before accepting their protocol behavior.
No replacement for #1758 productive owner ingress, #1811 source/resource/input proof or full #1703 CLI/Discord/fault/soak acceptance.

build_order.exit: Resolve or reject all load-bearing threads using primary kernel documentation, actual disposable races and source writer inventory. Independent fresh-eyes and seam audits triaged; no handoff until then.
Test-first real producer/consumer implementation with fault injection at every durable and permission boundary; no caller-controlled permission bits or reports mint authority.
Exact-head review and hosted CI, normal protected merge, managed snapshot and updater deployment. No production quota/floor change.

Apply through authenticated command to an actually eligible retained session, verify bytes/aliases/controls intact, actual bounded capacity recovered and one normal guarded native call advances. Continue broader epic acceptance.

tests_required: The actual open-unlinked writer control must prevent the real R resource-bound factory/accounting consumer from granting a small reservation, unless that resource is covered by a separately verified kernel bound whose demand remains reserved. Visible flags, read leases, metadata-only names and a journal alone must not pass.
Real file writer and writable mapping (including mapping after closing its FD) prevent a custody grant; unsupported leases and break signals refuse.

Deterministic delayed opens before/after permission checks, old constructor/host helper starts, FD duplication, chmod paths, partial permission changes, inode/path replacement and symlink/hardlink attacks cannot produce an unsound zero/small-growth grant.

For the immutable candidate, test real exact-host and declared-guest behavior plus concurrent multi-file directory/file transitions, preexisting writable FDs and prefaulted mappings, directory-entry races, flag/inode substitution, nonprivileged flag-clearing refusal, privileged helper authentication and crash durability. Serial guest success cannot satisfy this combined producer/consumer gate.

After a genuine credit permits a second real admission, invalidate the first receipt/fence or compatibility support and verify full demand is restored, the overcommit is reported, all new growth gates refuse, original active resources remain owned through checked teardown, and no data, hold, allowance or outcome is reset. Repeat across controller restart and lost replies.
Crash/lost reply before/after intent, each mode change, fsync, receipt commit and helper death preserves exact content and conservative accounting until proof is re-established.

A genuine metadata-only fixture can enter custody and reduce only future growth after all live proof gates, while an active session, exported/completed/unsettled result or unsupported file layout is retained conservatively.

Resume, cleanup, alias observation, old helpers and ordinary terminal retirement cannot undo custody or delete unknown data. Actual current admission revalidates the fence even if scheduling used an earlier report.
All budget/count/floor/owner/merge/source/input invariants remain unchanged; no provider/model call in resource-custody handling.
Live acceptance verifies the deployed current implementation and actual retained-state disposition; disposable syscall success alone is not restoration.
